oldValue: Wandering monsters often offer little treasure compared with the resources spent fighting them.
Negotiation or avoidance can be useful alternatives to combat.
newValue: Wandering monsters often offer little treasure compared with the resources spent fighting them.
Negotiation or avoidance can be useful alternatives to combat.
For an Appendix C dungeon character-party encounter, roll d4 + 1 for 2–5 characters; accompanying men-at-arms or henchmen bring the total party to nine.

In that encounter procedure, men-at-arms accompany parties on dungeon levels 1–3; on level 4 or deeper the companions are henchmen. Character-class incompatibilities and per-party class maxima must also be applied using the source table.

changes.oldValue: Gap: the different underlying person/monster charm-breaking schedules are not reproduced here.
changes.newValue: Charm person checks for a new saving throw by Intelligence: 3 or less every 3 months; 4–6 every 2 months; 7–9 monthly; 10–12 every 3 weeks; 13–14 every 2 weeks; 15–16 weekly; 17 every 3 days; 18 every 2 days; 19 or more daily. Charm monster has a weekly chance to break by monster level or HD: 1st/up to 2, 5%; 2nd/up to 3+2, 10%; 3rd/up to 4+4, 15%; 4th/up to 6, 25%; 5th/up to 7+2, 35%; 6th/up to 8+4, 45%; 7th/up to 10, 60%; 8th/up to 12, 75%; 9th/over 12, 90%.
changes.reason: Mass Charm explicitly refers to Charm Person and Charm Monster; their printed spell entries provide the separate schedules.
